name: Kubernetes component version skew policy: how far apart component versions can be in a supported cluster
description: The maximum version difference Kubernetes supports between cluster components, one record per governed component pair (kube-apiserver to kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, and the kube-controller-manager/kube-scheduler/cloud-controller-manager group, plus the kube-apiserver-to-kube-apiserver HA rule and the kube-proxy-to-kubelet rule), from the project's own version-skew-policy page. Answers 'how many minor versions behind can my kubelet be', 'can kubectl be newer than kube-apiserver', 'what must already be upgraded before I upgrade this component'. Getting this wrong during a rolling upgrade breaks node registration or blocks the upgrade path, usually discovered mid-rollout. The rule text is stable in structure release to release; the version numbers in the worked examples move with each Kubernetes minor release, so the numeric examples need re-verification on that cadence.
licence: Source is the Kubernetes project's own documentation (kubernetes.io), a CNCF project. The page footer reads 'Documentation Distributed under CC BY 4.0'. We take the fact plus a short attributed quote linking back.

records.skew_rule: the newest and oldest kube-apiserver instances must be within one minor version
records.newer_component_allowed: symmetric - the page bounds the gap between the newest and oldest instance without naming a governed side
records.worked_example: newest kube-apiserver is at 1.37 other kube-apiserver instances are supported at 1.37 and 1.36
records.upgrade_prerequisite: In a single-instance cluster, the existing kube-apiserver instance is 1.36 In an HA cluster, all kube-apiserver instances are at 1.36 or 1.37
records.source_quote: the newest and oldest kube-apiserver instances must be within one minor version.

records.component_pair: kube-apiserver and kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, or cloud-controller-manager
records.skew_rule: They are expected to match the kube-apiserver minor version, but may be up to one minor version older (to allow live upgrades).
records.newer_component_allowed: no - these components must not be newer than the kube-apiserver instances they communicate with
records.worked_example: kube-apiserver is at 1.37 kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, and cloud-controller-manager are supported at 1.37 and 1.36
records.ha_cluster_caveat: If version skew exists between kube-apiserver instances in an HA cluster, and these components can communicate with any kube-apiserver instance in the cluster (for example, via a load balancer), this narrows the allowed versions of these components.
records.upgrade_prerequisite: The kube-apiserver instances these components communicate with are at 1.37
records.source_quote: kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, and cloud-controller-manager must not be newer than the kube-apiserver instances they communicate with. They are expected to match the kube-apiserver minor version, but may be up to one minor version older (to allow live upgrades).

records.skew_rule: kube-proxy may be up to three minor versions older than kube-apiserver
records.newer_component_allowed: no - kube-proxy must not be newer than kube-apiserver
records.legacy_version_exception: kube-proxy < 1.25 may only be up to two minor versions older than kube-apiserver
records.worked_example: kube-apiserver is at 1.37 kube-proxy is supported at 1.37, 1.36, 1.35, and 1.34
records.ha_cluster_caveat: If version skew exists between kube-apiserver instances in an HA cluster, this narrows the allowed kube-proxy versions.
records.upgrade_prerequisite: The kube-apiserver instances kube-proxy communicates with are at 1.37
records.source_quote: kube-proxy must not be newer than kube-apiserver. kube-proxy may be up to three minor versions older than kube-apiserver (kube-proxy < 1.25 may only be up to two minor versions older than kube-apiserver).

records.skew_rule: kubectl is supported within one minor version (older or newer) of kube-apiserver.
records.newer_component_allowed: yes - kubectl is supported one minor version older or newer than kube-apiserver
records.worked_example: kube-apiserver is at 1.37 kubectl is supported at 1.38, 1.37, and 1.36
records.ha_cluster_caveat: If version skew exists between kube-apiserver instances in an HA cluster, this narrows the supported kubectl versions.
records.source_quote: kubectl is supported within one minor version (older or newer) of kube-apiserver.

records.skew_rule: kubelet may be up to three minor versions older than kube-apiserver
records.newer_component_allowed: no - kubelet must not be newer than kube-apiserver
records.legacy_version_exception: kubelet < 1.25 may only be up to two minor versions older than kube-apiserver
records.worked_example: kube-apiserver is at 1.37 kubelet is supported at 1.37, 1.36, 1.35, and 1.34
records.ha_cluster_caveat: If version skew exists between kube-apiserver instances in an HA cluster, this narrows the allowed kubelet versions.
records.upgrade_prerequisite: The kube-apiserver instances the kubelet communicates with are at 1.37
records.source_quote: kubelet must not be newer than kube-apiserver. kubelet may be up to three minor versions older than kube-apiserver (kubelet < 1.25 may only be up to two minor versions older than kube-apiserver).

records.skew_rule: kube-proxy may be up to three minor versions older or newer than the kubelet instance it runs alongside
records.newer_component_allowed: yes - kube-proxy may be older or newer than the kubelet instance it runs alongside
records.legacy_version_exception: kube-proxy < 1.25 may only be up to two minor versions older or newer than the kubelet instance it runs alongside
records.source_quote: kube-proxy may be up to three minor versions older or newer than the kubelet instance it runs alongside (kube-proxy < 1.25 may only be up to two minor versions older or newer than the kubelet instance it runs alongside).
